faq.q: What is the weather like in Sotogrande in June 2037?
faq.a: June 2037 in Sotogrande brings average highs of 27°C, sea temperatures around 22°C, and 12 hours of daily sunshine. Winds are typically light from the southeast at 10-15 knots, creating calm seas ideal for yacht charters. Rainfall is rare, with only 2-3 rainy days expected all month.

faq.q: How far is Sotogrande from Puerto Banús?
faq.a: Sotogrande is about 15 nautical miles south of Puerto Banús, a 40-50 minute cruise depending on your boat speed. Our fleet departs from Puerto Banús, so you'll enjoy a scenic coastal ride past Cabopino and Estepona before arriving at Sotogrande's marina.

faq.q: Which boats can I charter for a Sotogrande trip in June 2037?
faq.a: All our boats depart from Puerto Banús and can reach Sotogrande. For a fast trip, the Pershing 46 (14m, 10 pax) or Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) are great. For smaller groups, the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m, 5 pax) work well. Larger groups can book the Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax).

faq.q: What is included in the charter price?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) start at €749 for 2 hours. Tier B boats (Mangusta 80) cost €4,719 for a minimum 4 hours and include a free jet ski.

faq.q: Can I anchor near Sotogrande for swimming?
faq.a: Yes, the waters off Sotogrande offer several calm anchorages, especially near the Guadiaro River mouth or along the coast towards Cala del Faro. In June, the Mediterranean is warm (22°C) and clear, perfect for swimming. Your skipper will pick the best spot based on wind and sea conditions.

faq.q: Do I need to book in advance for June 2037?
faq.a: June is peak season in Sotogrande, so we recommend booking 2-4 weeks ahead. Popular boats like the Mangusta 80 and Azimut 58 Flybridge fill up quickly. Contact us via WhatsApp for availability and to secure your preferred date.

faq.q: What is the dress code for a yacht charter in June?
faq.a: Light summer clothing: swimwear, shorts, T-shirts, a sun hat, sunglasses, and non-marking shoes. Bring a light jacket for evening breezes. Sunscreen with SPF 50+ is essential. The skipper will provide towels if needed.

faq.q: Are there any restrictions on bringing food or drinks?
faq.a: You are welcome to bring your own food and additional drinks. Our standard charter already includes water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks. If you want a full catering service, let us know when booking – we can arrange it for an extra fee.

data.body_html:
Planning a sotogrande yacht charter june 2037? June is the start of peak season on the Costa del Sol, and Sotogrande offers some of the most exclusive anchorages in the region. With average temperatures of 27°C, 12 hours of sunshine, and calm seas, it's the perfect month to explore from the water. Our fleet of luxury yachts departs from Puerto Banús, just 15 nautical miles north – a 40-50 minute cruise past Cabopino and Estepona. Whether you want a fast Pershing 46 or a spacious Ferretti 94, we have the boat for your group.

June 2037 Weather Overview for Sotogrande

June in Sotogrande is hot, dry, and sunny. Expect daytime highs averaging 27°C, occasionally touching 30°C. Sea surface temperatures hover around 22°C – warm enough for comfortable swimming. Winds are light, typically from the southeast at 10-15 knots, creating gentle swells of less than 0.5 metres. Rainfall is minimal: only 2-3 rainy days on average. UV index is high (8-9), so bring strong sunscreen. The water visibility is excellent, often exceeding 15 metres.

Best Boats for a Sotogrande Charter in June

All our boats depart from Puerto Banús and can easily reach Sotogrande. For speed and style, the Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) or Pershing 46 (14m, 10 pax) are popular. For larger groups, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) offers luxury and includes a free jet ski. If you prefer a more intimate trip, the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m, 5 pax) are budget-friendly options. For a full list, see our fleet page.

What to Expect: Weather and Sea Conditions

In June 2037, the Mediterranean off Sotogrande is at its best. Morning sea breezes are light, building to 10-15 knots by midday. The sea state is typically slight to moderate (Douglas scale 2-3), making for a smooth ride. Afternoon thunderstorms are extremely rare. Sunset is around 21:30, giving you long evenings to enjoy a sunset cruise back to Puerto Banús. Visibility is excellent – you'll see the Sierra Bermeja mountains clearly from the water.

Pricing and Booking for June 2037

Our Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) start at €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours – all inclusive. Tier B boats (Mangusta 80 in white or grey) cost €4,719 for a minimum 4 hours, with a free jet ski. For all other boats (e.g., Ferretti 94, Pershing 46, Canados 86), pricing is on request via WhatsApp. We recommend booking 2-4 weeks ahead for June. Contact us to secure your preferred date.

Itinerary Ideas for a Sotogrande Yacht Charter

Start from Puerto Banús, cruise south past the Golden Mile and Estepona. Arrive at Sotogrande after 40-50 minutes. Anchor near the Guadiaro River mouth for swimming and lunch. Explore the Sotogrande Marina for a waterfront meal, then head to Cala del Faro for a quiet afternoon swim. Return to Puerto Banús in the late afternoon, catching the sunset over La Concha mountain. You can also extend to Cala Cortés or even Cabo de Gata if you have a full-day charter.
